heroHeadline: Zelensky Approves 40-Day SSU Operation to Pressure Russia — EU Extends Sanctions Through Summer 2027
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,564, Russia escalated to nuclear-site targeting: a Shahed drone struck the spent fuel-reception building at Chornobyl's nuclear fuel storage facility (~02:00 local), causing structural damage and a 40m² fire — no radiation release, but the IAEA announced an emergency site visit and Zelensky condemned the attack as 'extremely vile.' Separately, Russia launched 236 drones overnight (215 intercepted), killing 4 people across Ukraine. Ukraine's response was multifaceted: a second massive Kronstadt Naval Base strike overnight June 5–6 (~376 drones) hit the Baltic Fleet's 15th Arsenal at Bolshaya Izhora (secondary detonations confirmed) and the Research Institute of Marine Thermal Engineering (submarine weapons R&D), on the final day of Putin's SPIEF. In Crimea, Ukrainian SOF struck both the Feodosia maritime oil terminal (7 tanks ablaze) and the Semykolodezyanska oil depot in Kerch district (9 tanks), while a drone also damaged the Chonhar bridge — suspending the critical Crimea-mainland supply crossing. Ukraine's 3rd SOF Regiment had announced aerial drone control over the Melitopol–Chonhar corridor on June 6, making the bridge strike the culmination of a deliberate multi-day logistics attrition campaign. Diplomatically: Putin met Schröder at the Kremlin as proposed mediator (rejected by Kallas and Kyiv); a 500-POW exchange proceeding as part of the June 2 direct talks agreement. Russian military casualties reached ~1,373,500 (Ukraine MoD). Ukraine's 2026 energy strike campaign total exceeds $11B in Russian losses.
